title: Ring maps out of a field of characteristic p lift along nilpotent ideals of F_p-algebras
statement: Let $K$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$. Let $D$ be a commutative ring with $p\cdot1_D=0$, let $J\subseteq D$ be an ideal with $J^N=0$ for some integer $N\ge1$, let $\pi:D\to D/J$ be the quotient map, and let $g:K\to D/J$ be a ring homomorphism. Then there is a ring homomorphism $f:K\to D$ with $\pi\circ f=g$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0320 (lemma-formally-smooth-extensions-easy, line 44409), part (3): a separable field extension is formally smooth (Definition Tag 00TI, definition-formally-smooth, line 37805: lifting along square-zero ideals), applied to K over F_p, which is separable because F_p is perfect (Definition Tag 030Y, definition-perfect, line 10489; Lemma Tag 030Z, lemma-perfect, line 10495: every element of F_p is a p-th power); the passage from J^2=0 to J^N=0 by lifting successively along D/J^{i+1} -> D/J^i, as in the proof of Algebra Lemma Tag 07K4 (lemma-smooth-strong-lift, line 38291). Used in Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FG (smoothing.tex lines 2468-2470, 2489-2490, 2496-2497). Tags verified in literature/stacks-project/tags/tags
